Change c0535. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. VII; 1831 Ch. XXIV.

Context before (unchanged): His voice seemed suffocated; and my first impulses, which had suggested to me the duty of obeying the dying request of my friend, in destroying his enemy, were now suspended by a mixture of curiosity and compassion.

1818 text: I approached this tremendous being; I dared not again raise my looks upon his face, there was something so scaring and unearthly in his ugliness.

1831 text: I approached this tremendous being; I dared not again raise my eyes to his face, there was something so scaring and unearthly in his ugliness.

Diff: I approached this tremendous being; I dared not again raise my [-looks upon-] {+eyes to+} his face, there was something so scaring and unearthly in his ugliness.

Context after (unchanged): I attempted to speak, but the words died away on my lips.

result.rationale: Replaces 'raise my looks upon his face' with 'raise my eyes to his face'; same meaning and action, only a more idiomatic phrasing of the same gesture.
